notes:
## Content and scope
This sheet begins with two disjoint bands J and L, J preceding L, inside I prime, with J an ideal and L a coideal. It defines J prime as I prime minus L and writes an inclusion of ideals. Two diagrams relate the indexed X objects and their boundary ideals, each square marked cart. The lower display identifies the Sigma objects using complements involving the interior tube over I prime subscript0. The final sentence begins the consideration of a tubular neighbourhood of Sigma_J in Sigma_I prime and continues beyond the sheet.

The slanted upper margin expressly says that the writer is not very sure the disjointness or precedence hypotheses are essential. Its final reduced phrase, provisionally en fait on, remains uncertain; no grammatical completion has been supplied. The mathematical margin defines T_J, its interior and boundary, then gives two direct-limit expressions with authorial question marks above the equalities. The third upright equality in the lower display also has an authorial question mark.

## Image-driven rereadings prompted by mathematics
The ideal chain prompted a closer reading of the crowded word before d'idéaux. Its dotted initial i and tall l support inclusion, C's alternative, rather than suite. The proof or correctness of the chain was not checked. The three top objects of the first diagram prompted comparison of the rightmost subscript with the adjacent I prime and middle J prime: the right-hand subscript has a right stem and leftward foot and is read as barred J prime, despite the preceding X_I prime. This is a possible authorial index slip, preserved from the ink rather than corrected to fit the parallel pattern.

The diagrams' apparent inclusions prompted inspection of every connector. All have left or bottom hooks and no arrowheads. Their literal shapes are drawn in TikZ without choosing an implied arrow direction. The three lower starred objects of the first diagram remain on a separate row, joined by short upright equalities. H's note recognizes some of these features, but its diagram code does not consistently preserve them.

The first and second limit conditions were both reread in full. Each writes est between d and the membership sign; this is retained even though the symbol already expresses membership. The final-element condition begins with a repetition dash instead of repeated letters él. Its next short word is canceled; est remains only a narrow uncertain reading. Both limit signs have clear rightward arrowheads. The canceled T definition remains uncertain beneath its overwrite, and the irregular decoration above the union's final T_j cannot safely be called a clean bar, dot or absence of accent.

Every agreed formula was checked visually as well: prime positions, bars and tilde, the disjointness signs, the three boundary-ideal definitions and all three final interior-T terms. Both written J-intersection-L equalities use a phi-shaped loop crossed by a stem in the local upright writing direction. They are transcribed literally as phi against C's varnothing and H's emptyset; their possible empty-set meaning is not used to substitute another glyph. No mathematical proof verification, independent re-proof, formal calculation or use of these statements has been performed.

## Physical page
There is no title, date or numbered equation. The authorial upper-left number is 39 in the main brown hand. The lower-left 85 is a thin grey foliation from another hand and remains a margin item. The sheet contains three genuine diagrams, two marginal note streams, three cancellation sites and no independently marked insertion. The underlined disjointes remains underlined. There are 40 counted manuscript lines/graphic rows including the two stand-alone numbers; see line_count_note for the explicit basis.

The corrected packet's 57 diff rows, D0296 through D0352, are all covered. Earlier malformed parsed structures were discarded when the parent supplied the corrected differences field; no extraneous-page material was used. Whole-page viewing was followed by each supplied native half once. The first attempted half1 output was truncated and not counted; the successful displayed half1 and half2 were read. All 21 saved crops were inspected, including the corrected full foliation85 framing. The record describes visual collation only.
### Blind reading corrections

The opening marginal phrase remains partly unresolved: Je ne suis pas is clear, but the reduced following group is now marked très sûr/sûr. The page visibly divides vrai- / ment. The marginal definitional label is unaccented def. The blotted decoration of the first T_j is now represented by canceled-circle/dot alternatives rather than an asserted overbar candidate. The middle T in the lower diagram also has a filled-looking raised mark and now carries a ring/dot doubt. All three diagrams retain the observed headless hooked strokes, upright relation pairs and the literal upper-right J-prime subscript. The blind alternatives did not justify replacing that written J with the expected I. No additional mathematical claim was checked by these readings.
